purpose: Static SY1 GUI design mockups; no application implementation

prompts.name: filter
prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a polished, practical GUI mockup for SY1, a hardware synthesizer with a small square 240x240 color display and FOUR PHYSICAL ENCODERS below the display. This is a screen design proposal, not code.
Show ONLY the square screen artwork filling the image, straight-on and flat. No hardware enclosure, hands, perspective, surrounding desk, browser chrome, poster titles, or extra screen. Output a square high-resolution enlargement designed with a real 240x240 logical pixel grid in mind.
Shared design language across the set: Nord Modular G2 inspired hardware clarity and playfulness. Near-black charcoal #151719 background; warm ivory #f4efdf text; restrained vivid red #ed493f accents; amber #ffc967 for the value being edited; muted grey for secondary marks. No rainbow. Crisp clean typography, bold legible values; avoid ultra-small dense text. No glows, glass, photographic textures, gradients, fake screws, or ornamental UI.
Fixed layout: top 42 logical pixels contain a small patch identifier "P02", the name "Warm Pad" in bold and a small amber edited dot. Next, a thin red section strip with the page label. The middle is a large, simple visual of the sound parameter, around 85 logical pixels high. The lower 77 logical pixels are exactly FOUR equal control columns, visibly mapped left-to-right to physical encoders 1 to 4: parameter name above a small segmented semicircular indicator, big value below. These indicators are feedback glyphs, not big 3D virtual knobs. Thin understated separators. The currently edited column has a warm dark tinted background and amber indicator/value. A tiny notch marks saved position separately from current setting. Bottom 17 logical pixels: a small MIDI activity dot, "3/8", and "120 BPM". No touch buttons or mouse cursors.
Text must be exact, with clear hierarchy and enough space to be legible on the tiny screen. Inviting, playable, professionally coherent embedded instrument interface.
Page label "FILTER". Middle visual: a low-pass filter frequency response, warm ivory horizontal passband then a clear resonance peak and descending steep cutoff slope; faint red dashed curve shows the prior saved setting. Two small frequency labels only, "100" and "10k". The current cutoff has an amber marker labelled "2.4k" above it. Control columns exactly: "TYPE" / "LP24"; "CUTOFF" / "2.4k"; "RESO" / "42"; "ENV" / "+35". Column 2 is active. Keep cutoff chart large and easy to understand. It should clearly show that turning encoder 2 changes cutoff.
